title: The devil's trick and the question of painted images
english: The devil contrived idolatry in the world by his own evil art, sowed it in the world and established it, and turned human beings away from God. Now again, after the heresies and the idols, he has dragged the faithful down into the ancient idolatry and deceived them. Epiphanius brings himself forward in the letter as having followed the faith of the fathers at Nicaea from his youth, and as having parents who were born in that faith and held the same confession. For your piety will understand whether it is fitting for us to have a painted God made with colors. I have heard that some even promise to paint the incomprehensible Son of God; I do not recall ever seeing such a thing.
Which of the ancient fathers painted an image of Christ and set it up in a church or in his own house, or on the curtains of doors?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Epistula ad Theodosium imperatorem u01-open
orientation: Epiphanius opens his letter to the emperor by describing how the devil introduced idolatry and now deceives believers, then begins questioning whether any ancient father painted an image of Christ.
